$comment: Generated by scripts/sync-tools.mjs from a Bytebase instance's built-in MCP server. Do not edit by hand; rerun `npm run sync-tools`.
instructions:
Bytebase governs access to databases and changes to them. Every call is also limited by the workspace's MCP access policy.

Choose the tool by task:
- Find a database: call_api(operationId="DatabaseService/SearchDatabases") lists the databases you can view.
- Read data: query_database. Before you write SQL for a database, read its schema with get_schema.
- Inspect a schema: get_schema.
- Change a database: propose_database_change, the easiest way into the governed workflow. It creates the plan and the issue and runs the plan checks; approval and rollout follow the project's policy. It changes one database per call. For several databases in one plan, ask the user to use the Bytebase console or GitOps.
- Anything else: a tool whose description covers the task; failing that, search_api to find the operation and its request schema, then call_api.

When the workspace's MCP access policy is Read-write, query_database can also run DML and DDL, as far as the engine and the account's permissions allow; call_api refuses them. They take effect at once, without an issue or approval. Use propose_database_change for any change that should be reviewed, or when a write fails on a read-only data source.

When Bytebase refuses a call, the error states the reason and may name a next step, such as a tool to use.

tools.name: administer_workspace
tools.description:
Make a workspace administration change that the user confirms in this client first. It takes a Bytebase API operation and its request body, as search_api describes them.

| Parameter   | Required | Description |
|-------------|----------|-------------|
| operationId | Yes      | The operation, e.g. "SettingService/UpdateSetting" |
| body        | Yes      | The operation's request body |

It serves four changes.

The approval rules for database changes: send SettingService/UpdateSetting with setting.name "settings/WORKSPACE_APPROVAL" and the whole rule list in setting.value.workspaceApproval.rules. Read the stored rules first with call_api SettingService/GetSetting, change only the rules whose source is CHANGE_DATABASE, and send every other rule as stored, in its order. Give each rule you add the source CHANGE_DATABASE. Send a rule's source, condition.expression, template.title, template.description and template.flow.roles; other fields are refused. Name each approver in template.flow.roles by its role name, such as roles/workspaceDBA. An approval check tries the CHANGE_DATABASE rules in order, and the first whose condition matches decides who approves a change. When none matches, the rules with no source, such as the Fallback Rule, decide, and a change that no rule matches needs no approval.

The masking rules: send OrgPolicyService/UpdatePolicy with policy.name "workspaces/{workspace}/policies/masking_rule", policy.type MASKING_RULE and the whole rule list in policy.maskingRulePolicy.rules, with allowMissing true when no rules are stored yet. Read the stored rules first with call_api OrgPolicyService/GetPolicy, and the semantic types with call_api SettingService/GetSetting on settings/SEMANTIC_TYPES; the built-in types bb.default (full mask) and bb.default-partial (partial mask) always exist. Send a rule's id, condition.expression, condition.title and semanticType; other fields are refused, and the tool sets updateMask. Keep each stored rule's id, and give each new rule a new UUID. Masking tries the rules in order, and the first whose condition matches gives a column its semantic type; a column that no rule matches keeps its own.

A PostgreSQL instance in a project: send InstanceService/CreateInstance with parent "projects/{project}", instanceId, and instance with title, engine POSTGRES, environment ("environments/{id}", or left out for none), activation, and one dataSources entry: type ADMIN, host, port, username, password, and optionally database, useSsl, verifyTlsCertificate and authenticationType PASSWORD; the tool sets its id. Other fields are refused, keys that name no field are ignored, and the default project cannot own an instance. Masking skips an instance that is not activated unless every instance is licensed; the create refuses activation true when no license is free, as on the Free plan. When the user accepts, Bytebase tests the connection and adds the instance only if it connects; its databases join the project for good.

A workload identity for CI jobs in one GitHub or GitLab repository: send WorkloadIdentityService/CreateWorkloadIdentity in a project, with the fields search_api's note on it lists. When the user accepts, the tool creates it and grants it the GitOps Service Agent role in the project.

The tool shows the user what changes and asks them to confirm in a form. It makes the change only when they accept; declining or cancelling changes nothing. Do not ask in chat first: the form is the question.

Reading and changing the approval rules needs bb.settings.get and bb.settings.set, as in the console. Reading and changing the masking rules needs bb.policies.getMaskingRulePolicy and bb.policies.updateMaskingRulePolicy, bb.policies.createMaskingRulePolicy for the first save, and bb.settings.get for the semantic types. Adding an instance needs bb.instances.create, and a workload identity bb.workloadIdentities.create, bb.projects.getIamPolicy and bb.projects.setIamPolicy. call_api refuses each of these writes.

tools.name: call_api
tools.description:
Execute a Bytebase API endpoint. **Use search_api first to get operationId and schema.**

| Parameter | Required | Description |
|-----------|----------|-------------|
| operationId | Yes | e.g., "SQLService/Query" |
| body | No | JSON request body |

**Resource names:** Preserve the exact canonical name returned by SearchDatabases or ListDatabases:
instances/prod/databases/main for a workspace instance, or
projects/my-project/instances/prod/databases/main for a project instance.

**Example:**
call_api(operationId="SQLService/Query", body={"name": "projects/my-project/instances/i/databases/db", "statement": "SELECT 1"})

tools.name: decide_issue
tools.description:
Approve or reject a Bytebase issue at its current approval step. The user confirms the decision in this client first.

| Parameter | Required | Description |
|-----------|----------|-------------|
| issue     | Yes      | Issue name, e.g. "projects/hr/issues/42" |
| decision  | Yes      | "approve" or "reject" |
| comment   | No       | Note recorded with the decision |

The tool shows the user what the issue changes and asks them to confirm in a form. It decides only when they accept; declining or cancelling changes nothing. A client that cannot show the form gets the issue's link, to decide it in the Bytebase console instead. Do not ask in chat first: the form is the question.

It decides database changes and access requests. Role requests stay in the Bytebase console, because approving one grants a project role.

The approval rules decide who may approve, as in the console: the user must hold the role of the current step, and approving their own issue, or a plan they last changed, is refused unless the project allows it.

This is the only way to decide an issue over MCP; call_api refuses IssueService/ApproveIssue and RejectIssue.

tools.name: get_gitops_workflow
tools.description:
Return the workflow files that set up GitOps for a project. With them in the repository, every pull request that changes the migration folder gets a Bytebase SQL review, and merging it deploys. The tool reads only; it changes nothing in Bytebase.

| Parameter        | Required | Description |
|------------------|----------|-------------|
| project          | Yes      | The project ID, e.g. "hr" |
| targets          | Yes      | One database group ("projects/hr/databaseGroups/all"), or one or more databases by the name ListDatabases gives ("instances/prod/databases/hr") |
| workloadIdentity | Yes      | The email of the workload identity the jobs sign in as |
| folder           | No       | The folder that holds the migration files. Default "migrations" |

To set up GitOps from the team's repository:
1. Read the repository. The git remote gives the provider (GitHub or GitLab), the owner and the repository. Look for the folder that holds the SQL migration files.
2. Ask the owner which databases to deploy to. List the project's database groups and databases with call_api (DatabaseGroupService/ListDatabaseGroups, DatabaseService/ListDatabases). Offer a group first: a database that joins it later is deployed with no change to the files, when its environment is one the files already deploy to.
3. Find the workload identity with call_api WorkloadIdentityService/ListWorkloadIdentities on the project. Use one whose subject pattern names this repository. If there is none, create one with administer_workspace.
4. Call this tool. Write each file at its path, and on GitLab add the include line the result gives to .gitlab-ci.yml. Ask before you replace a file that exists. Open a pull request into the default branch.

The jobs sign in with their own ID token, so the repository needs no secret. The workflows run only when a file in the migration folder changes, so the setup pull request runs neither, and the first pull request with a migration file is the test. With the GitOps Service Agent role, the identity's rollouts carry no issue, so no approval rule holds them: tell the owner that merging deploys.

You may fit the files to the repository, for example the runner, the stages, or how they join an existing pipeline. Keep BYTEBASE_URL, BYTEBASE_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY, the job permissions, the ID token settings, the action image, --project, --targets and the order of the deploy jobs. The identity admits every job in the repository, so the triggers alone decide which branch deploys: tell the owner before a change that lets another branch deploy.

tools.name: get_schema
tools.description:
Inspect a Bytebase database's schema.

| Parameter | Required | Description |
|-----------|----------|-------------|
| database  | Yes      | Database name or substring (e.g., "employee_db" or "employee") |
| instance  | No       | Workspace instance ID/name, or the full canonical name for a project instance |
| project   | No       | Project name or ID to narrow resolution |
| schema    | No       | Schema name for multi-schema engines (PG/MSSQL/Oracle/Snowflake/Redshift/CockroachDB/Databricks/Trino/Spanner/Hive); ignored with a note on MySQL/TiDB/etc. |
| table     | No       | Drill into a single table; implies include="details" |
| include   | No       | Detail level: "summary" (default), "columns", "details" |

**Usage:**
- First call: get_schema(database="employee") → compact overview
- Drill down: get_schema(database="employee", table="orders") → full table detail
- Write a query: get_schema(database="employee", include="columns") → all tables with columns

**Notes:**
- Metadata is auto-synced on access. The first call to a stale database may take longer.
- For databases with many tables, columns/details modes return up to 200 tables PER SCHEMA.
  Use schema= or table= to narrow further.
- Column masking metadata is only returned when table= is set.
- rowCountEstimate is the row count the last metadata sync recorded. It can be an estimate, and can read 0 for a table that has rows; run a COUNT query when the number matters.
- Requires bb.databases.getSchema permission.

tools.name: grant_masking_exemption
tools.description:
Exempt one member from data masking in a Bytebase project, for one database (optionally one schema, table, or columns of one table) or for every database in the project. The user confirms the exemption in this client first.

| Parameter    | Required | Description |
|--------------|----------|-------------|
| project      | Yes      | Project name, e.g. "projects/hr" |
| member       | Yes      | "user:{email}", "group:{email}", "serviceAccount:{email}" or "workloadIdentity:{email}" |
| database     | One of   | Database name, e.g. "instances/prod/databases/hr"; it must belong to the project |
| allDatabases | One of   | true for every database in the project, current and future |
| schema       | No       | Narrow to one schema (needs database) |
| table        | No       | Narrow to one table (needs database) |
| columns      | No       | Narrow to these columns of the table, e.g. ["first_name", "last_name"] (needs table) |
| expireTime   | No       | RFC 3339 time the exemption ends, e.g. "2026-10-27T00:00:00Z"; without it, it does not expire |
| reason       | No       | Why, recorded with the exemption |

An exemption is a standing policy change: the member bypasses the masking that applies to the covered data in query and export results, including masking set up later. It does not set up masking itself; administer_workspace changes the masking rules. For a one-off query, request an access grant instead with request_access_grant.

The tool adds one exemption and leaves every other entry as it is. For several columns of one table, pass them together in columns, so the user confirms once. It shows the user the member, the scope, the expiry and the effect, and asks them to confirm in a form; it writes only when they accept. A client that cannot show the form gets the project's masking exemption page, to grant it in the Bytebase console instead. Do not ask in chat first: the form is the question.

The same permissions apply as in the console. This and revoke_masking_exemption are the only ways to change exemptions over MCP; call_api refuses OrgPolicyService/UpdatePolicy.

tools.name: propose_database_change
tools.description:
Run DDL/DML changes (ALTER TABLE, CREATE TABLE, INSERT, UPDATE, migrations) against a Bytebase database.

This is the primary tool for making database changes. Use this instead of manually calling CreateSheet/CreatePlan/CreateIssue via call_api.

Provide plain SQL — the tool handles database resolution, sheet creation, plan creation with automatic plan checks, and issue creation in one call. Optionally creates a rollout.

| Parameter     | Required | Description |
|---------------|----------|-------------|
| database      | Yes      | Database name or substring |
| sql           | Yes      | SQL statement(s) in plain text (NOT base64) |
| title         | Yes      | Title for the issue/plan |
| instance      | No       | Workspace instance ID/name, or the full canonical name for a project instance |
| project       | No       | Project name or ID to narrow resolution |
| changeType    | No       | "MIGRATE" (default) or "SDL" |
| createRollout | No       | If true, attempts rollout creation after issue |
| reason        | No       | Context or ticket reference (max 1000 chars) |

**Examples:**
propose_database_change(database="app", sql="ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN status VARCHAR(20)", title="Add status column")
propose_database_change(database="app", sql="UPDATE orders SET status='shipped' WHERE id=42", title="Ship order 42", createRollout=true)

**Notes:**
- It changes one database per call. For several databases in one plan, ask the user to use the Bytebase console or GitOps.
- Plan checks run automatically; results included in response when available.
- Requires bb.sheets.create, bb.plans.create, bb.issues.create permissions.
- If createRollout=true but policy gates aren't satisfied, returns success with rolloutCreated=false and a reason.
- nextAction AWAIT_HUMAN_APPROVAL means the issue waits for its approvers. If the user is one of them, decide_issue asks them to confirm in this client and then approves; otherwise share links.issue with an approver.
- Masked data: a masked column reads back as "******". That is a placeholder, not a value anything holds. Any change containing it is refused, because writing it back would overwrite the real value. Ask a human to make the change in the Bytebase console instead.

tools.name: query_database
tools.description:
Execute a SQL query against a Bytebase database. Resolves the database by name automatically.

| Parameter | Required | Description |
|-----------|----------|-------------|
| database  | Yes      | Database name or substring (e.g., "employee_db" or "employee") |
| statement | Yes      | SQL query to execute |
| instance  | No       | Workspace instance ID/name, or the full canonical name for a project instance |
| project   | No       | Project name or ID to narrow resolution |
| schema    | No       | Default schema for unqualified names (Postgres search path). An access grant applies only when this equals the grant's schema |
| container | No       | CosmosDB container (required for CosmosDB). An access grant applies only when this equals the grant's container |
| limit     | No       | Max rows (default: 100, max: 1000) |
| issueTitle | No      | For a statement that may write: the issue's title if the user chooses Create an issue. The form shows it in that choice. Say what the change does, without data values. Without it, the form does not offer Create an issue |

**Examples:**
query_database(database="employee_db", statement="SELECT * FROM users LIMIT 10")
query_database(database="employee", instance="prod-pg", statement="SELECT count(*) FROM orders")
query_database(database="employee", instance="projects/hr/instances/prod-pg", statement="SELECT count(*) FROM orders")
query_database(database="employee_db", statement="UPDATE employee SET active = false WHERE id = 42", issueTitle="Deactivate an employee")

**Notes:**
- Show the user the statement each answer came from, so they can check it read what they asked about.
- When the user asks for an issue or a review of a change, call propose_database_change instead. It takes no schema, so when the request named one, qualify each name with it.
- Masked data: masking replaces a value fully (by default "******"), partly (e.g. "**rn**"), or with a hash. maskedColumns in the result names each masked column and why (not reported for MongoDB, CosmosDB or Elasticsearch). A masked value is a placeholder, not a value anything holds, so never write it back and never filter on it. Any statement containing "******" is refused. When showing a partly masked value, wrap it in backticks: "**rn**" renders as bold Markdown.
- Seeing masked values: the user can ask a project owner for a masking exemption, or, if the project allows just-in-time access, request an access grant with Unmask for this exact statement, schema and container. In a Read-write session, file the request with request_access_grant; otherwise the user requests it in the SQL Editor. Once it is approved, find the grant among the user's access grants, then rerun the granted statement unchanged with the grant's schema and container. appliedAccessGrant in the result names the grant that applied.

tools.name: reauthorize
tools.description:
Log out the current MCP OAuth connection so the client can run OAuth again.

Use this when you need to change the connected Bytebase account or SaaS workspace. After this tool succeeds, retry the MCP request or reconnect; the server will return the normal OAuth challenge.

tools.name: request_access_grant
tools.description:
Request an access grant: time-boxed permission to run one read-only statement on one Bytebase database, optionally with results unmasked or exported. A person approves the request in Bytebase before it takes effect.

| Parameter     | Required | Description |
|---------------|----------|-------------|
| database      | Yes      | Full database name, as query_database prints it after "Database:", e.g. "projects/hr/instances/prod/databases/hr" |
| statement     | Yes      | One read-only statement; the grant applies to this exact statement |
| schema        | No       | Default schema for unqualified names; the rerun must pass the same one |
| container     | No       | CosmosDB container; the rerun must pass the same one |
| unmask        | No       | true to return masked columns unmasked |
| export        | No       | true to allow exporting the results |
| reason        | Yes      | Why the access is needed; the approver reads it |
| durationHours | Yes      | Hours of access, counted from approval. The SQL Editor offers 1, 4, 24 and 168; the workspace maximum applies |

The project must allow just-in-time access. Check allowJustInTimeAccess with call_api(operationId="ProjectService/GetProject") first; a missing field means off, and set_just_in_time_access turns it on.

Clients such as Claude Code ask the user to approve each call of this tool, so do not ask in chat first. Once the request is approved, rerun the statement unchanged with query_database, with the same schema and container; appliedAccessGrant in its result names the grant that applied. To use an export grant, pass the statement the same way to call_api(operationId="SQLService/Export"); query_database returns at most 1000 rows.

tools.name: revoke_masking_exemption
tools.description:
Remove one member's masking exemption in a Bytebase project. The user confirms in this client first.

| Parameter | Required | Description |
|-----------|----------|-------------|
| project   | Yes      | Project name, e.g. "projects/hr" |
| member    | Yes      | The member as the policy lists it, e.g. "user:bob@example.com" |
| condition | Yes      | The exemption's condition expression, exactly as OrgPolicyService/GetPolicy returns it for "{project}/policies/masking_exemption"; "" for an exemption with no condition |

The member is removed from every exemption whose condition matches exactly; an exemption left with no member is removed. Other members and other exemptions stay as they are. The tool asks the user to confirm in a form, and writes only when they accept. A client that cannot show the form gets the project's masking exemption page.

The same permissions apply as in the console.

tools.name: search_api
tools.description:
Discover Bytebase API endpoints. **Always call before call_api - never guess schemas.**

| Mode | Parameters | Result |
|------|------------|--------|
| List | (none) | All services |
| Browse | service="SQLService" | All endpoints in service |
| Details | operationId="SQLService/Query" | Request/response schema |
| Schema | schema="Instance" | Message type definition |

**Workflow:** search_api() → search_api(service="...") → search_api(operationId="...") → call_api(...)

The results also name what no MCP session can do, whatever the workspace's MCP mode and the user's permissions, and why: those are done in the Bytebase console.

tools.name: set_just_in_time_access
tools.description:
Turn just-in-time access on or off for one Bytebase project. The user confirms the change in this client first.

| Parameter | Required | Description |
|-----------|----------|-------------|
| project   | Yes      | Project name, e.g. "projects/hr" |
| enabled   | Yes      | true to turn it on, false to turn it off |

Just-in-time access lets members request access grants in the project: time-boxed permission to run one statement, for a one-off query. With it off, new requests are refused, and active grants stop applying until it is turned on again; they are not revoked.

The tool shows the user the change and asks them to confirm in a form. It changes the setting only when they accept; declining or cancelling changes nothing. A client that cannot show the form gets the project's settings link, to change it in the Bytebase console instead. Do not ask in chat first: the form is the question.

Changing it needs bb.projects.update, as in the console. This is the only way to change it over MCP; call_api refuses ProjectService/UpdateProject.
